description: Make RunnerGrain's work-timeout reminder register-if-absent so additional work assignments do not reset its due-time, keeping timeout scanning on a stable cadence while outstanding work exists.

tasks.title: Make work-timeout reminder register-if-absent and add scheduling-behavior tests
tasks.description: Modify `EnsureWorkTimeoutReminderAsync` in `packages/server/src/Mohist.Server/Runner/Grains/RunnerGrain.cs` to be register-if-absent: call `this.GetReminder(WorkTimeoutReminderName)` first and only call `RegisterOrUpdateReminder` when the reminder does not already exist, so subsequent work assignments via `PollOneWorkflowAsync`/`AssignAgentJobAsync` no longer reset the reminder's due-time. Keep the call sites unchanged (they still call `EnsureWorkTimeoutReminderAsync` after recording outstanding work) and leave the drain-side unregister path (`MaybeUnregisterWorkTimeoutReminderAsync`) untouched. Per-work deadline basis (`CreatedAt`/`TakenAt`) and the `failed(reason=timeout)` synthesis path via `ReportWorkflowResultAsync` are unchanged.
acceptanceCriteria: `EnsureWorkTimeoutReminderAsync` performs a `GetReminder` existence check before any `RegisterOrUpdateReminder`, returning early (no reminder-table write) when the `work-timeout` reminder already exists (Decision 1).

The first assignment that transitions outstanding work from zero to non-zero registers the `work-timeout` reminder; `PollOneWorkflowAsync` and `AssignAgentJobAsync` call sites remain unchanged and do not call `RegisterOrUpdateReminder` directly.

Reminder scheduling is verified by querying the reminder table (resolve `IReminderService`/`IReminderTable` from the silo via `Cluster.GetSiloServiceProvider`): after the first assignment a `work-timeout` row exists for the runner grain id; after a second assignment while the reminder exists the row's `StartAt` is unchanged (proves no due-time reset); after drain the row is gone; after drain + new work a row exists again (fresh `StartAt`).

An end-to-end behavioral test covers the older-work scenario: poll W1, advance the fake clock near (but under) `WorkCompletionTimeout`, assign W2, then advance just past W1's deadline and drive the reminder tick — asserts W1 synthesizes `WorkResult(status="failed", reason="timeout")` via the `ReportWorkflowResultAsync` channel while W2 remains outstanding, proving W2's assignment did not postpone W1's judgment.
A test covers scanner lifecycle when outstanding work drains to zero (reminder unregistered) and later new work reappears (reminder re-registered with register-if-absent semantics).
At least one test drives the behavior through the reminder (`ReceiveReminder` / in-memory reminder service tick) rather than only calling `CheckWorkTimeoutsAsync` directly (issue AC #7).

Existing drain behavior is preserved: a scan observing no pending/running work still unregisters/stops the reminder via `MaybeUnregisterWorkTimeoutReminderAsync`, and the reminder is not unregistered while outstanding work remains.

Existing reminder-persistence / orphan-work behavior (issue #275) remains intact — no change to the reminder name, period, `WorkCompletionTimeout` default (30 min), `RunnerWorks` ledger schema, or `failed/timeout` synthesis result.
`npm test` (server) passes; `TreatWarningsAsErrors` is clean. Web/runner typecheck are unaffected but run as part of CI gating.
tasks.output: Modified `packages/server/src/Mohist.Server/Runner/Grains/RunnerGrain.cs` (register-if-absent helper) plus new/extended reminder-scheduling tests in `packages/server/tests/.../Runner/Grain/RunnerWorkLedgerSpecs.cs` and/or `RunnerFailureSpecs.cs` (and a small fixture helper to read the in-memory reminder table if not already present).
tasks.notes: Single-method control-flow fix (Decision 1). Decision 2 (drain unregister) and Decision 4 (no state/schema/config change) are explicitly no-op. Decision 3 mandates two complementary test strategies: direct reminder-table assertion (intent-revealing check for the due-time-drift regression) + end-to-end behavioral assertion (user-visible older-work timeout). Implementation must NOT use an in-memory `_workTimeoutReminderRegistered` flag (rejected in design: desyncs on grain reactivation).
